photoobj_star_cohort.name: photoobj_star_cohort
photoobj_star_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec,
  p.type AS type,
  p.u AS u,
  p.g AS g,
  p.r AS r,
  p.i AS i,
  p.z AS z,
  p.clean AS clean
FROM
  photoobj p
WHERE
  p.objid IS NOT NULL
  AND p.clean IS NOT NULL
  -- do not hard-code the 'STAR' label here; question_ops will apply that filter using p.type and photo_type
photoobj_star_cohort.description: Cohort of photoobj rows that represent star-class photometric objects and have valid measurements (non-null objid and marked clean). Does not bake in the literal 'STAR' string filter; that goes in question_ops so the same cohort can be used for other types later.

photoobj_basic_photometrics.name: photoobj_basic_photometrics

specobj_to_photoobj_link.name: specobj_to_photoobj_link
specobj_to_photoobj_link.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid AS specobjid,
  s.bestobjid AS bestobjid,
  s.ra            AS "specobj.ra",
  s.dec           AS "specobj.dec",
  s.class         AS "specobj.class",
  s.z             AS "specobj.z",
  p.objid         AS "photoobj.objid",
  p.ra            AS "photoobj.ra",
  p.dec           AS "photoobj.dec",
  p.type          AS "photoobj.type"
FROM specobj s
LEFT JOIN photoobj p
  ON s.bestobjid IS NOT NULL
  AND p.objid = s.bestobjid
specobj_to_photoobj_link.description: Denormalized mapping between specobj and its best-matching photoobj (if any) via specobj.bestobjid -> photoobj.objid. Exposes basic spectroscopic and photometric identifiers to support star classification cross-checks and future joins between spectra and imaging.

photoobj_with_spec_match.name: photoobj_with_spec_match

photoobj_with_spec_match.description: Denormalized row-level relation of photometric objects that have at least one linked spectroscopic record (via specobj.bestobjid), exposing photo identifiers and coordinates alongside the matching specobj id.

photoobj_core_positions.name: photoobj_core_positions
photoobj_core_positions.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonical object id: carry through photoobj.objid as object_id
  p.objid AS object_id,

  -- normalized right ascension: non-finite -> NULL, ensure double precision
  (CASE WHEN p.ra IS NULL THEN NULL
        WHEN p.ra = 'Infinity'::double precision OR p.ra = '-Infinity'::double precision THEN NULL
        WHEN p.ra = 'NaN'::double precision THEN NULL
        ELSE p.ra::double precision END) AS right_ascension,

  -- normalized declination: non-finite -> NULL, ensure double precision
  (CASE WHEN p.dec IS NULL THEN NULL
        WHEN p.dec = 'Infinity'::double precision OR p.dec = '-Infinity'::double precision THEN NULL
        WHEN p.dec = 'NaN'::double precision THEN NULL
        ELSE p.dec::double precision END) AS declination

FROM photoobj AS p
photoobj_core_positions.description: Canonical photometric object records with core identifying and positional columns normalized (casts/NULL-cleaning). One row per photoobj.objid.

specobj_core_links.name: specobj_core_links
specobj_core_links.body_sql:

specobj_core_links.description: Canonical spectral observation rows exposing specobj primary identifiers and the linked photometric object id (bestobjid). One row per specobj.specobjid.

photo_with_spectrum_join.name: photo_with_spectrum_join

FROM

photo_with_spectrum_join.description: Denormalized rows of photometric objects that have at least one linked spectrum (via specobj.bestobjid = photoobj.objid). One row per photoobj.objid per matching specobj.specobjid.

photoobj_galaxy_cohort.name: photoobj_galaxy_cohort
photoobj_galaxy_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid::bigint AS objid,
  p.ra::double precision AS ra,
  p.dec::double precision AS dec,
  p.u::real AS u,
  p.g::real AS g,
  p.r::real AS r,
  p.i::real AS i,
  p.z::real AS z,
  p.clean::integer AS clean,
  p.type::integer AS type,
  pt.name::character varying AS photo_type_name
FROM photoobj_with_type p
JOIN photo_type pt
  ON pt.value = p.type
WHERE
  -- Lifted literals: photo_type name to match 'GALAXY'
  pt.name = 'GALAXY'
  -- Basic quality filters (photometric usable object)
  AND p.clean IS NOT NULL
  AND (p.clean & 0) = 0  -- placeholder to allow fast-bitmask extension in downstream filters; does not change rows
  AND p.type IS NOT NULL
  -- require reasonable positions
  AND p.ra BETWEEN 0 AND 360
  AND p.dec BETWEEN -90 AND 90
  -- require non-null primary photometry (r is commonly primary)
  AND p.r IS NOT NULL
  -- extinction available (useful for later calibration)
  AND p.extinction_r IS NOT NULL
photoobj_galaxy_cohort.description: Denormalized cohort of photoobj rows whose type corresponds to photo_type classification(s) identified as 'GALAXY', with positional and photometric columns and basic quality filters applied. Intended as a reusable galaxy-observable cohort for further filtering/aggregation.

photo_type_lookup_17.name: photo_type_lookup_17
photo_type_lookup_17.body_sql:

photoobj_with_spec_match_18.name: photoobj_with_spec_match_18
photoobj_with_spec_match_18.body_sql:

  p.dec   AS dec,
  s.specobjid   AS specobjid,
  s.bestobjid   AS spec_bestobjid,
  s.ra          AS spec_ra,
  s.dec         AS spec_dec
FROM photoobj p
JOIN specobj s
  ON p.objid = s.bestobjid
   OR p.objid = s.specobjid
photoobj_with_spec_match_18.description: Denormalized relation linking photometric objects to spectroscopic observations when present. One row per photoobj.objid and one row for each matching specobj where photoobj.objid equals specobj.bestobjid or specobj.specobjid. Enables filtering to objects that have spectra.

specobj_by_bestobjid.description: Spectroscopic observations keyed by the photometric object they were best-matched to (specobj.bestobjid). Useful to determine whether a photoobj has a directly associated spectrum and to expose spec metadata.

neighbors_linked_to_specobj.name: neighbors_linked_to_specobj
neighbors_linked_to_specobj.body_sql:
SELECT
  n.objid                    AS objid,
  n.neighborobjid            AS neighborobjid,
  n.distance                 AS distance,
  n.type                     AS type,
  n.mode                     AS mode
FROM
  neighbors n
JOIN
  photoobj p1
    ON n.objid = p1.objid
JOIN
  photoobj p2
    ON n.neighborobjid = p2.objid
JOIN
  specobj s
    ON s.bestobjid = p2.objid
WHERE
  -- liftable literal: exclude NULL distances (keep explicit predicate as example)
  n.distance IS NOT NULL
neighbors_linked_to_specobj.description: Neighbor links that connect photometric objects to other photometric objects; can be used to find indirect associations between a photoobj and another object that has a spectrum (via specobj.bestobjid).

photoobj_with_type_label.name: photoobj_with_type_label

photoobj_with_type_label.description: Denormalized mapping of photoobj rows to human-readable photo type labels from photo_type; one row per photometric object with its type code and type name.

photoobj_galaxy_candidates.name: photoobj_galaxy_candidates
photoobj_galaxy_candidates.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.type
FROM
  photoobj p
WHERE
  -- photometric galaxy type codes: lift literals out of view if reused elsewhere
  p.type IN (3, 4)
  -- ensure row-level photometric detection (optional basic clean filter lifted here)
  AND (p.clean IS NULL OR (p.clean & 0) = 0)
photoobj_galaxy_candidates.description: Cohort of photoobj rows identified as photometric galaxies (type-coded) at row-level; does not apply spatial bounding so can be reused for spatial or other filters later.

photoobj_photometric_positions.name: photoobj_photometric_positions
photoobj_photometric_positions.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.type,
  p.clean,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  p.extinction_r,
  p.run,
  p.field,
  -- compute camcol from integer division of 'colc' into 6 camera columns (1..6).
  -- Lift literal '6' out: number of camcols = 6
  ( (floor((p.colc)::numeric / NULLIF( ( (p.colc)::numeric + 0 ) / ( (p.colc)::numeric + 0 ) , 1) )::int % 6) + 1 )::int AS camcol,
  p.mjd
FROM photoobj_rows p
photoobj_photometric_positions.description: Canonical projection of photoobj rows exposing positional and photometry-clean columns used for spatial and star/cohort filters. Keeps raw magnitudes and flags for downstream filters.

neighbors_pairs_with_distance.name: neighbors_pairs_with_distance

photoobj_specobj_joined.name: photoobj_specobj_joined
photoobj_specobj_joined.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid AS specobjid,
  p.objid      AS objid,
  COALESCE(p.ra, s.ra)   AS ra,
  COALESCE(p.dec, s.dec)  AS dec,
  s.z           AS z,
  s.class       AS class
FROM
  specobj s
LEFT JOIN
  photoobj p
ON
  s.bestobjid = p.objid
photoobj_specobj_joined.description: Denormalized rows joining spectroscopic observations to their best-matching photometric object, yielding one row per spectroscopic observation with photometric coordinates and IDs for spatial queries and analysis.

  s.loadversion
FROM specobj s
specobj_canonical.description: Canonical spectroscopic object rows exposing specobj primary key, bestobjid (link to photometry), spectroscopic classifications, redshift and quality metrics. No domain-specific literal filters so it can be reused for class-based or quality-based cohorts.
validated_on: Show me the object id, right ascension, declination, and redshift of spectroscopic observed galaxy in a certain area, of which the right ascension is in an unbouded interval of 185 and 186, declination is in an unbouded interval of 15 and 16.
Find the object id, right ascension and declination of spectroscopic Galaxy, which have value of magnitude g between 17 and 18 and redshift less than 0.05.
counter_examples: Fetch me the object id, right ascension and declination of spectroscopic Galaxy with the color band magnitude g brighter than 18.0 but fainter than 17 and redshift lower than 0.05

photoobj_with_spec_joined.name: photoobj_with_spec_joined
photoobj_with_spec_joined.body_sql:
SELECT

  p.clean AS clean,
  p.flags AS flags,
  p.rowc AS rowc,
  p.colc AS colc,
  p.cmodelmag_u AS cmodelmag_u,
  p.cmodelmag_g AS cmodelmag_g,
  p.cmodelmag_r AS cmodelmag_r,
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec,
  p.b AS b,

  p.extinction_r AS extinction_r,

  p.loadversion AS loadversion,
  p.u AS u,
  p.g AS g,

LEFT JOIN specobj s

photoobj_with_spec_joined.description: Denormalized join of photometric objects to their matched spectroscopic records (when available) using specobj.bestobjid = photoobj.objid. Exposes all columns from photoobj and specobj to support queries that need both photometry and spectroscopy. This view is one row per photoobj.objid joined to at most one specobj (specobjid) when present.

photo_spec_join_by_bestobjid.name: photo_spec_join_by_bestobjid
photo_spec_join_by_bestobjid.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid::numeric AS specobjid,
  s.bestobjid::bigint AS bestobjid,
  p.objid::bigint AS objid,
  COALESCE(p.ra, s.ra) AS ra,
  COALESCE(p.dec, s.dec) AS dec,

  s.class::text AS class,
  p.clean::integer AS clean
FROM specobj AS s
LEFT JOIN photoobj AS p
  ON s.bestobjid = p.objid
photo_spec_join_by_bestobjid.description: Denormalized one-row-per-specobj join between spectroscopic records and their matched photometric object (via specobj.bestobjid = photoobj.objid), exposing both photometric position/mags and spectroscopic redshift/class for spatial+spectral queries.

photoobj_star_photometry.name: photoobj_star_photometry
photoobj_star_photometry.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  p.type,
  p.clean,
  p.run,
  p.field
FROM photoobj_rows p
WHERE
  -- ensure basic photometry present (lifted literals)
  p.u IS NOT NULL
  AND p.g IS NOT NULL
  AND p.r IS NOT NULL
  AND p.i IS NOT NULL
  AND p.z IS NOT NULL
  -- require positional info
  AND p.ra IS NOT NULL
  AND p.dec IS NOT NULL
  -- keep only objects with a valid type and clean flag (clean > 0 typically)
  AND p.type IS NOT NULL
  AND p.clean IS NOT NULL
photoobj_star_photometry.description: All photo-detected objects with available photometric magnitudes and basic positional and classification columns; useful as a base cohort of observed sources (optionally restricted to stars by applying a type value in question_ops).

photoobj_color_indices.name: photoobj_color_indices
photoobj_color_indices.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra   AS ra,
  p.dec  AS dec,
  p.u    AS u,
  p.g    AS g,
  p.r    AS r,
  p.i    AS i,
  p.z    AS z,
  -- color indices computed from stored magnitudes; lift no literals here
  (p.u - p.g) AS u_minus_g,
  (p.g - p.r) AS g_minus_r,
  (p.r - p.i) AS r_minus_i,
  (p.i - p.z) AS i_minus_z
FROM
  photoobj p
photoobj_color_indices.description: Per-photoobj canonical color index projections (u-g, g-r, r-i, i-z) computed from stored magnitudes; retains original magnitudes and positional keys so it can be joined/filtered efficiently.
counter_examples: What is the star in photometrically observed binary star system, of which the neighbor's distance is less than 0.05 and has the following constraints in its color bands, u - g < 0.4, g - r < 0.7, r - i > 0.4 and i - z > 0.4

photoobj_with_neighbor_counts.name: photoobj_with_neighbor_counts
photoobj_with_neighbor_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  COALESCE(nc.neighbor_count, 0) AS neighbor_count,
  nc.nearest_neighbor_distance AS nearest_neighbor_distance
FROM
  photoobj p
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    n.objid AS objid,
    COUNT(*) AS neighbor_count,
    MIN(n.distance) AS nearest_neighbor_distance
  FROM
    neighbors n
  GROUP BY
    n.objid
) nc
  ON p.objid = nc.objid
photoobj_with_neighbor_counts.description: Per-photoobj neighbor summary: counts of neighbor objects and minimum neighbor distance; useful for identifying isolated vs blended detections and for quality filters in selection queries.

photoobj_photometry_canonical.name: photoobj_photometry_canonical
photoobj_photometry_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  -- lift literal defaults out of view: none here; simply pass through cleaned/normalized columns
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  -- normalize clean: treat non-positive or NULL as NULL, otherwise keep as-is
  CASE WHEN p.clean IS NULL THEN NULL
       WHEN p.clean < 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE p.clean END AS clean,
  -- flags: ensure integer type (bigint preserved) and NULL-clean
  CASE WHEN p.flags IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE p.flags END AS flags,
  -- position centroids: propagate NULLs unchanged
  CASE WHEN p.rowc IS NULL OR p.rowc = 'NaN'::real THEN NULL ELSE p.rowc END AS rowc,
  CASE WHEN p.colc IS NULL OR p.colc = 'NaN'::real THEN NULL ELSE p.colc END AS colc,
  -- cmodel mags: coerce unreasonable sentinel values (e.g. very large magnitudes) to NULL; keep numeric otherwise
  CASE WHEN p.cmodelmag_u IS NULL OR p.cmodelmag_u > 90 THEN NULL ELSE p.cmodelmag_u END AS cmodelmag_u,
  CASE WHEN p.cmodelmag_g IS NULL OR p.cmodelmag_g > 90 THEN NULL ELSE p.cmodelmag_g END AS cmodelmag_g,
  CASE WHEN p.cmodelmag_r IS NULL OR p.cmodelmag_r > 90 THEN NULL ELSE p.cmodelmag_r END AS cmodelmag_r,
  -- i and z cmodel mags are not present in photoobj DDL; derive as NULL to keep schema stable
  NULL::real AS cmodelmag_i,
  NULL::real AS cmodelmag_z,
  -- PSF (or aperture) mags: use provided columns, null-clean similarly
  CASE WHEN p.u IS NULL OR p.u > 90 THEN NULL ELSE p.u END AS u,
  CASE WHEN p.g IS NULL OR p.g > 90 THEN NULL ELSE p.g END AS g,
  CASE WHEN p.r IS NULL OR p.r > 90 THEN NULL ELSE p.r END AS r,
  CASE WHEN p.i IS NULL OR p.i > 90 THEN NULL ELSE p.i END AS i,
  CASE WHEN p.z IS NULL OR p.z > 90 THEN NULL ELSE p.z END AS z,
  -- astrometry
  CASE WHEN p.ra IS NULL OR p.ra = 'NaN'::double precision THEN NULL ELSE p.ra END AS ra,
  CASE WHEN p.dec IS NULL OR p.dec = 'NaN'::double precision THEN NULL ELSE p.dec END AS dec,
  -- extinction in r-band: null-clean and keep as real
  CASE WHEN p.extinction_r IS NULL OR p.extinction_r < 0 THEN NULL ELSE p.extinction_r END AS extinction_r,
  -- mjd: keep integer or NULL
  CASE WHEN p.mjd IS NULL OR p.mjd < 0 THEN NULL ELSE p.mjd END AS mjd
FROM photoobj AS p
photoobj_photometry_canonical.description: Canonical normalized photometry and basic detection metadata from photoobj with explicit null-cleaning and standardized numeric column names to be used by color and quality filters.
validated_on: Find the object id, right ascension and declination of spectroscopic Galaxy, which have value of magnitude g between 17 and 18 and redshift less than 0.05.
counter_examples: Show me the photometrically observable star with the color band magnitude i brighter than 19 but fainter than 0, the difference of magnitude g and r is greater than 2.26, the difference of magnitude i and z is less than 0.25, and either the difference of magnitude u and g is greater than 2.0 or the color band magnitude u is fainter than 22.3

neighbors_pair_distances.name: neighbors_pair_distances
neighbors_pair_distances.body_sql:
SELECT
  n.objid AS objid,
  n.neighborobjid AS neighborobjid,
  n.distance AS distance,
  n.type AS type,
  n.neighbortype AS neighbortype,
  n.mode AS mode,
  n.neighbormode AS neighbormode
FROM neighbors n
WHERE
  -- liftable literal: maximum distance to report; change as needed when creating the view
  n.distance IS NOT NULL
  AND n.distance <=  '5.0'::double precision
  -- Exclude self-neighbors if present
  AND n.objid IS DISTINCT FROM n.neighborobjid
neighbors_pair_distances.description: Pairwise neighbor relationships between detections with distance and role/type/mode flags; useful to filter or deblend close neighbors or apply isolation criteria.
validated_on: Find all photometric observable GALAXY whose magnitude g is brighter than 22, the difference of magnitude u and magnitude g is between -0.27 and 0.71, the difference of magnitude g and magnitude r is between -0.24 and 0.35, the difference of magnitude r and magnitude i is between -0.27 and 0.57 and the difference of magnitude i and magnitude z is between -0.35 and 0.7. Retrieve the object id and magnitude g with descent order by magnitude g.
counter_examples: What is the star in photometrically observed binary star system, of which the neighbor's distance is less than 0.05 and has the following constraints in its color bands, u - g < 0.4, g - r < 0.7, r - i > 0.4 and i - z > 0.4

photoobj_star_photometry_41.name: photoobj_star_photometry_41
photoobj_star_photometry_41.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid::bigint AS objid,
  p.run::smallint AS run,
  p.rerun::smallint AS rerun,
  p.field::smallint AS field,
  p.mode::smallint AS mode,
  p.type::smallint AS type,
  p.clean::integer AS clean,
  -- canonicalized positions (use photoobj values; pass-through)
  p.ra::double precision AS ra,
  p.dec::double precision AS dec,
  -- Photometry: prefer calibrated magnitudes (u/g/r/i/z) from photoobj_basic_photometrics if available,
  -- otherwise fall back to photoobj's u/g/r/i/z. Lifted literals: none.
  COALESCE(b.u, p.u) AS u,
  COALESCE(b.g, p.g) AS g,
  COALESCE(b.r, p.r) AS r,
  COALESCE(b.i, p.i) AS i,
  COALESCE(b.z, p.z) AS z
FROM photoobj AS p
LEFT JOIN photoobj_basic_photometrics AS b
  ON p.objid = b.objid
photoobj_star_photometry_41.description: Canonicalized photometric measurements and identifying columns for objects classified as photos (photoobj). Converts/normalizes core magnitude and positional columns and exposes them for color calculations. Does not apply color cuts or distance/neighborhood filters so it can be reused for many selection tasks.

neighbors_per_object.name: neighbors_per_object
neighbors_per_object.body_sql:
SELECT
  n.objid,
  n.neighborobjid,
  n.distance,
  n.type,
  n.neighbortype,
  n.mode,
  n.neighbormode
FROM neighbors AS n
WHERE TRUE
  -- liftable literal example: allow filtering by a maximum distance by replacing '1.0' when creating or querying the view
  AND n.distance <= 1.0
neighbors_per_object.description: Row-level neighbor relations: one row per (objid, neighborobjid) pair with separation and relation-type metadata. Useful to filter by proximity thresholds or to find close companions.

photoobj_with_close_neighbors.name: photoobj_with_close_neighbors
photoobj_with_close_neighbors.body_sql:
SELECT

Keeps full photometry for the primary object and neighbor id + distance for proximity checks. Does NOT collapse multiple neighbors; one row per neighbor pair.

photoobj_with_neighbor_info.name: photoobj_with_neighbor_info
photoobj_with_neighbor_info.body_sql:

photoobj_with_type_46.name: photoobj_with_type_46

photo_type_lookup_47.name: photo_type_lookup_47

photoobj_with_type_48.name: photoobj_with_type_48

photoobj_with_type_label_49.name: photoobj_with_type_label_49

photo_type_lookup_50.name: photo_type_lookup_50
photo_type_lookup_50.body_sql:
SELECT
  pt.value AS value,
  pt.name AS name,
  pt.description AS description
FROM (
  -- lift literals out: define the mapping rows here as VALUES
  -- One row per distinct photoobj.type integer code used in the catalog
  -- (examples provided; extend later without changing view logic)
  VALUES
    (0, 'Unknown', 'Type not specified'),
    (1, 'Galaxy', 'Extended source; galaxy-like morphology'),
    (2, 'Star', 'Point source; star-like morphology'),
    (3, 'Sky', 'Sky measurement / background'),
    (4, 'CosmicRay', 'Cosmic ray detection'),
    (5, 'Satellite', 'Satellite / artifact'),
    (6, 'Asteroid', 'Moving object / asteroid'),
    (7, 'Deblended', 'Deblended child object'),
    (8, 'Blend', 'Blended parent object')
) AS pt(value, name, description)
photo_type_lookup_50.description: Lookup table mapping photo type integer codes to semantic names and descriptions (e.g., 'Galaxy', 'Star'). Useful for filtering by object class without hard-coding type integers.

photoobj_colors.name: photoobj_colors
photoobj_colors.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  -- lift any literals out: none needed here
  (p.u - p.g) AS u_minus_g,
  (p.g - p.r) AS g_minus_r,
  (p.r - p.i) AS r_minus_i,
  (p.i - p.z) AS i_minus_z
FROM photoobj p
photoobj_colors.description: Per-photoobj computed color columns (adjacent magnitude differences) for easy color-based cohort selection. Does not apply color-range filters itself.

photoobj_star_type_codes.name: photoobj_star_type_codes

SELECT

This view does not hardcode a specific mapped value; consumers should filter where name = 'STAR' in question_ops.

photoobj_pos_and_class.name: photoobj_pos_and_class

photoobj_color_measures.name: photoobj_color_measures
photoobj_color_measures.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,

  (p.u - p.g) AS u_minus_g,
  (p.g - p.r) AS g_minus_r,
  (p.r - p.i) AS r_minus_i,

photoobj_color_measures.description: Computed color columns per photoobj to simplify color-based selections (u-g, g-r, r-i, i-z). This is a row-level view (no grouping aggregation) that exposes derived color metrics.

photo_type_lookup_55.name: photo_type_lookup_55

photo_type_lookup_56.name: photo_type_lookup_56

photoobj_join_specobj_by_bestobjid.name: photoobj_join_specobj_by_bestobjid
photoobj_join_specobj_by_bestobjid.body_sql:

photoobj_join_specobj_by_bestobjid.description: Denormalized mapping of photometric objects to their matched spectroscopic records (via specobj.bestobjid = photoobj.objid), exposing both photometry and spectroscopy for each linked photoobj row.

photoobj_with_spec_match_58.name: photoobj_with_spec_match_58
photoobj_with_spec_match_58.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid                            AS objid,
  p.ra                                AS ra,
  p.dec                               AS dec,
  p.g                                 AS g,
  s.specobjid                         AS specobjid,
  s.class                             AS class,

    ON s.bestobjid = p.objid
photoobj_with_spec_match_58.description: Denormalized view of photometric objects joined to their matching spectroscopic record (specobj.bestobjid -> photoobj.objid) exposing both photo and spec fields useful for selection.
